issue.title: Lengthen the 60 s runner wait fallback once release telemetry shows >=90% non-fallback releases

task_type_fields.proposal:
After `sase update` deploys epic sase-1hf (wait lane repair), evaluate the new wait release telemetry and, if it qualifies, lengthen the parked runner's direct-resolution fallback.

1. Tally `wait_release_source` over a representative window (at least a day of runs) with the recipe in `docs/axe.md` ("Wait release telemetry"). Count only dependency releases: `ready_json` + `manual` versus `runner_fallback` (exclude `startup` and `timer`).
2. If at least 90% of dependency releases are non-fallback, raise `_WAIT_DEPENDENCY_FALLBACK_INTERVAL` in `src/sase/axe/run_agent_wait.py` from 60 s to 180-300 s. Update `tests/test_run_agent_wait_fallback.py` and the fallback wording in `docs/axe.md`.
3. If the share is below 90%, record the measured split and `wait_release_latency_s` p50/p95 on this bead and stop. The ready-json lane is still underperforming, so lengthening the fallback would slow releases.

Benefit: each fallback pass builds a full project dependency index (~5 s) per live waiter per minute. A longer interval removes most of that cost once `wait_checks` is the primary release path.

Proposed by phase bead sase-1hf.5 (lane-split) in PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #1, item 1. Filed by the sase-1hf land agent.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: The sase-1hf plan explicitly deferred this change. The report gates it on Phase 0 telemetry ("once >=90% of releases come via ready.json"), and that data cannot exist until the epic is deployed and has run for a while.

issue.creation_reason: sase-1hf deferred lengthening _WAIT_DEPENDENCY_FALLBACK_INTERVAL until its new wait_release_source telemetry proves wait_checks is the primary release path; this records the gated follow-up so the cost saving is not lost.
